posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
1 - When you have errors, the Sources tab is not useful to use - show a screenshot of the full Console tab.
2 - Please don't post several hundred lines of code directly into your post. If you must put it there, put spoiler tags around it - or just attach the file itself.
3 - This is not great practice, trying to shoehorn code not written for RPG Maker into your project. At first glance, it's making its own input handlers which are going to either overwrite or conflict with RPG Maker's built-in input mappers. If all you want is this Tetris game and it's already written, there's no need to shove it into RPG Maker.

And it is against forum rules to ask for help with fixing AI-generated code.

posts.author: ShadowDragon
posts.body:
e.code searches for keyL  keyA etc which personally is better.
as "which" is deprecated is some browsers and shouldn't be used.
code or keyCode is a better approach as I switch to e.code instead
as its supported for all browsers.
but I would go to the RPG maker code like ATT_Turan said, as input is available,
and overwriting it might break more things with other plugins which you don't
want either.
if your new to RPG Maker and its plugin, than learn the engine first before
making plugins, unless you know JS as you can learn the engine maybe
a bit faster to write plugins for it.
